Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
148 PM PST Tue Nov 24 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Outside of a few light showers in northeast California tonight
  into Wednesday, the forecast is dry and warmer, with favorable
  travel conditions for Thanksgiving.

* Pockets of freezing fog remain possible in the Martis Valley,
  Sierra Valley, and Mono Lake Basin overnight the morning hours
  the next several mornings.

* Rain and high elevation mountain snow return Sunday into Monday, 
  with a stronger and colder storm possible Tuesday into Wednesday 
  bringing the return of travel difficulties in the Sierra. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...

A Pacific storm is reaching the northern CA/southern Oregon coast as 
of the time of writing, but largely falls apart as it shifts inland. 
Low end precipitation chances (10-20%) remain in northeast 
California and far northern Washoe County near the Oregon border 
into Wednesday morning. Otherwise the moisture plume is pushed well 
to our north into the PacNW as a strong ridge builds into the west, 
keeping the region dry through the Thanksgiving Holiday.

This ridge will keep inversions in place for lower valley locations 
with minimal winds and chances for freezing fog in the Martis 
Valley, Sierra Valley, and Mono Lake Basin. Despite this, we'll 
still see warming across the region as compared to the recent cold. 
High temperatures will climb into the 50s both in western Nevada 
valleys and Sierra Valleys, with lows even above freezing in warmer 
valleys and midslopes this weekend.

Another wave of moisture arrives late Sunday into Monday, though is 
disjointed from the main low, which remains closer to the Washington 
coast. Precipitation chances are 50-80% in the Sierra and northeast 
CA, decreasing to 20-50% into western Nevada. The region remains on 
the warm side of the jet stream, with snow levels fairly high, 
generally near or above 7000 feet elevation, outside of areas near 
the Oregon border which will drop to 6500 feet, plus or minus 750
feet. Snow could still affect mountain passes in the Sierra, so 
anyone traveling on the back end of the holiday weekend should be 
prepared. Ridge winds will increase with this system as well, 
potentially affecting backcountry recreation.

Ensembles are starting to cluster in on a stronger and colder storm 
Tuesday night into Wednesday next week, with 90% of the ensemble 
meteograms showing at least some precipitation in the Sierra and 
western Nevada. The meteogram trends have been showing increasing
liquid and snow amounts, though 10th to 90th percentile ranges 
for snow levels are still wide, around 4500-6500 feet. In any 
event, plan for wintry weather if you are needing to traverse the 
Sierra next week. -Dawn

&&

.AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast: 

* VFR conditions with widespread mid to high level cloud cover and 
  light surface winds prevail into early Wednesday AM. 

* Increasing S-SW FL100 winds of 40-50 kts will bring periods of 
  LLWS from 03z to 08z this evening, along with increased 
  turbulence. Otherwise, light winds and VFR conditions expected 
  into the weekend, with slantwise visibility issues in the morning 
  due to strong inversions and haze.

Regional Outlook: 

* For KTRK, FZFG with periods of LIFR conditions from around 06z to 
  15z Wednesday. TVL has a chance for patchy shallow FZFG brings 
  brief MVFR/IFR conditions from 06z to 15z Wednesday. 

* Increasing S-SW FL100 winds of 40-50 kts will bring periods of 
  LLWS through 0800Z this evening for Lake Tahoe and western NV 
  terminals along with increased turbulence.

24-72 Hour Outlook: 

* VFR conditions with light winds continue through early Saturday, 
  except for FZFG potential with LIFR conditions at KTRK Thursday 
  and Friday mornings. Valley inversions may also lead to increased 
  haze buildup mainly around KRNO/KCXP/KMEV Thursday and Friday 
  mornings, with minor reductions in slantwise visibility.-McKellar
